text:
Monday, October 29, 2018
Get the Morning Brief sent directly to your inbox every Monday to Friday by 6:30 a.m. ET. Subscribe
What to watch today Will markets ever bounce back? On Friday, both the Dow and S&P 500 closed at levels putting them in red figures for 2018 and just above the level that would constitute correction territory, defined as a 10% drop from recent highs.
In the week ahead, investors will be greeted by another busy schedule with the monthly jobs report and marquee earnings from Apple ( AAPL ) and Facebook ( FB ) highlighting the schedule. Other notable companies expected to report results in the coming week include Akamai ( AKAM ), Constellation Brands ( STZ ), and KLA-Tencor ( KLAC ) on Monday; Facebook, General Electric ( GE ), Mastercard ( MA ), Aetna ( AET ), Coca-Cola ( KO ), Under Armour ( UAA ), Pfizer ( PFE ), and eBay ( EBAY ) on Tuesday; General Motors ( GM ), Kellogg ( K ), Yum Brands ( YUM ), and AIG ( AIG ) on Wednesday; Apple, Dow DuPont ( DWDP ), Church & Dwight ( CHD ), Zoetis ( ZTS ), Metlife ( MET ), CBS ( CBS ), and Starbucks ( SBUX ) on Thursday; and ExxonMobil ( XOM ), AbbVie ( ABBV ), and Chevron ( CVX ) on Friday.

Top news (Photo by Igor Golovniov/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) More IBM to acquire software company Red Hat : IBM Corp. ( IBM ) said on Sunday it had agreed to acquire U.S. software company Red Hat Inc. ( RHT ) for $34 billion, including debt, as it seeks to diversify its technology hardware and consulting business into higher-margin products and services. [Reuters]
Merkel to step down as CDU party leader : Angela Merkel, the most powerful woman in Europe, is standing down as the leader of her Christian Democratic Union party, according to German media reports. After holding the post for 18 years, she is allegedly standing down. [Yahoo Finance UK]
Baillie Gifford is willing to invest more in Tesla : One of the world’s largest fund managers and largest shareholders of Tesla ( TSLA ) has revealed that it is willing to invest more into Elon Musk’s electric car-maker. Nick Thomas, a partner at Edinburgh-based Baillie Gifford, said “if he (Tesla CEO Musk) needs more capital we would be willing to back him.” [Yahoo Finance UK]
US midterm elections will be both historically costly and pivotal : Republicans own a cash edge over Democrats going into U.S. midterm elections on November 6. Democrats, meanwhile, have outpaced Republicans by raising money from small donors for key house races. The match-up, expected to be the costliest congressional election cycle in history, will result in a pivotal day of voting in America. [Yahoo Finance]
UK budget: What to expect for taxes, pensions, more : The UK government’s highly anticipated budget will be unveiled on Monday, giving citizens insight into spending, taxing and borrowing plans. This is the final annual budget before the UK leaves the European Union in March 2019, and it comes as UK unemployment is at its lowest level in decades but economic growth is significantly below other developed nations. [Yahoo Finance UK]
China’s industrial profits growth slows for fifth month : P rofit growth at China’s industrial firms slowed for the fifth consecutive month in September as sales of raw materials and manufactured goods further ebbed, pointing to cooling domestic demand in the world’s second-biggest economy. [Reuters]
